claims.text: The initially solid FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles are compositionally homogeneous before heating.
Cu has a lower intrinsic melting point than Fe, Ni, Cr, and Co.
Thermal excitation causes Cu to preferentially segregate to nanoparticle surfaces and interfacial regions.
Cu segregation is caused by Cu's lower melting point relative to the other constituent elements.
Surface and interfacial Cu enrichment produces localized nanoscale liquid-phase domains before overall melting.
The localized liquid domains act as nucleation sites for subsequent overall melting.
Cu-rich liquid regions lower the activation barrier for the phase transition.
Cu segregation governs both the onset and progression of melting in FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles.
Baseline nanoparticles with nominal Cu content will show surface premelting at a lower temperature than Cu-reduced variants.
Early premelting in the baseline particles will appear as liquid-like domains in in-situ TEM and as broadened or lower-temperature DSC features.
Reducing Cu content by approximately 10–20% will delay and sharpen the melting onset and reduce signs of early liquid formation.
TEM and DSC are applicable techniques for characterizing HEA powders and their thermal behavior under argon.
The cited prior studies support preferential Cu segregation and Cu-driven premelting in binary or multicomponent nanoparticles.
Other constituent elements and atomistic diffusion kinetics could also influence the phase transition.
Baseline and Cu-reduced nanoparticles will be compared under identical inert-atmosphere heating cycles while particle size is held similar.
Failure to observe Cu segregation before melting, or failure to detect a statistically significant Cu-dependent change in melting behavior, will falsify the hypothesis.
